intro: SISGP 2027-28: the Swedish Institute's fully funded master's scholarship - tuition paid, SEK 12,000/month living allowance and SEK 15,000 travel grant. Scholarship window 8-24 February 2027.
description:
About the Scholarship

The Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals is Sweden's main government-funded master's scholarship. It targets future leaders - people who have already worked a few years and now want a master's degree in Sweden - and it is deliberately tied to leadership and sustainable development rather than pure academic merit. The Swedish Institute pays your university tuition directly, gives you a monthly allowance, and plugs you into an alumni network that keeps working in your favour long after graduation.

One structural point catches many applicants out: the scholarship is a two-step process. You must first apply to an eligible Swedish master's programme through universityadmissions.se (16 October 2026 to 15 January 2027), and only then - after you have your programme applications in - can you apply for the SISGP scholarship itself between 8 and 24 February 2027.

What the Scholarship Covers

Benefits
ComponentDetails
Tuition feesFull tuition paid directly by the Swedish Institute to your Swedish university, every semester.
Living allowanceSEK 12,000 per month throughout the study period.
Travel grantSEK 15,000 one-time payment (SEK 10,000 for scholars from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine; not applicable if you already live in Sweden).
InsuranceThe scholarship does not include insurance - check what coverage your university provides for fee-paying and scholarship students.
NetworkMembership of the SI Network for Global Professionals during studies and the SI Alumni Network afterwards.

Eligible Countries (34)

  • Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Egypt, Ethiopia
  • Georgia, Guatemala, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Liberia, Malaysia, Mexico, Moldova
  • Morocco, Nigeria, Peru, Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda
  • Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Zambia

Work Experience Requirement

Who qualifies
CriterionRequirement
CitizenshipCitizen of one of the 34 eligible countries listed above.
Work experienceAt least 3,000 hours of work experience before February 2027, accumulated from a maximum of three employers (management or leadership in NGO, government, business or academia counts).
Exempt countriesApplicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine must provide proof of work experience but are not held to the 3,000-hour minimum.
AdmissionYou must hold (or be awaiting) admission to an eligible Swedish master's programme applied for by 15 January 2027.

Application Timeline

Two steps, two windows
StageDates
Master's applications16 October 2026 - 15 January 2027 via universityadmissions.se
Scholarship application8 - 24 February 2027 (portal closes at 14:59 CET on 24 February)
SI screening25 February - 31 March 2027
Admission notifications1 April 2027 from University Admissions
Final scholarship decisions1 - 22 April 2027

How to Apply

Apply to your chosen master's programmes first, keep your application numbers handy, then complete the SISGP form in the February window with work-experience documentation, leadership evidence and motivation answers. The evaluation weighs professional experience and leadership potential alongside academics, so a supervisor's reference or employer letter that speaks to concrete impact is worth more here than another certificate.

About the Swedish Institute

The Swedish Institute is a government agency working to create interest in Sweden and build relationships with other countries through scholarship programmes, cultural exchange and public diplomacy. Its scholarship portfolio covers master's study, research fellowships and short professional programmes.

Official Link

  • Official advert and application (verified link)
  • SISGP official programme page (deadlines and rules)

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 24 February 2027 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
